# 6. Cell visualization

**Module 06 — Cell visualization.** 2D and 3D single-cell graph plots using
pixelatorR's `cell_plot` visualization framework. This shows *where* proteins sit on a
single cell's surface graph (clustering, polarization and colocalization patterns
that population-level scores in module `04` summarise but don't show directly). Run
after module `02`. See the [cell visualization tutorial](https://software.pixelgen.com/pna-analysis/R/tutorials/cell_visualization/)
for more detail.

```{r}
#| label: module06_setup

library(here)
here::i_am("modules/06_cell_visualization.qmd")

source(here::here("modules", "common_setup.R"))

if (!exists("pg_data", inherits = TRUE)) {
  pg_data <- load_checkpoint("annotated_seurat_object.rds")
}
```

## 6.1. Parameters

> **Decision checkpoint** (set the cell type and markers to plot). 
> In practice, cell visualization is an interactive process, where you select cells and markers of interest based on prior knowledge and/or analysis results and then plot them - often in multiple ways. The example presented here uses CD8 T cells and the CD82/CD81 pair, which often colocalize on the cell surface. 

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_parameters

cell_type_of_interest <- "CD8 T"            # one value from `cell_annotation`
markers_to_viz        <- c("CD82", "CD81")  # markers to render on the graph
n_cells               <- 4                  # cells to show in the 2D grid
```

## 6.2. Select cells

How you pick cells depends on what you want to show — the shape of typical cells, a
polarized marker, a colocalization pattern, or a cell–cell conjugate. Below we just
take a few cells of one type; change the selection to suit your question.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_select_cells

# Sample `n_cells` cells from the cells of interest
set.seed(42)
cells_of_interest <-
  WhichCells(pg_data, expression = cell_annotation == cell_type_of_interest) |>
  sample(n_cells)

if (length(cells_of_interest) == 0) {
  stop("No cells found for '", cell_type_of_interest,
       "'. Check the values in `cell_annotation`.")
}
```

## 6.3. Load graphs and compute layouts

We load the cell graphs and compute the layouts for the cells of interest.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_layout

pg_data <- RemoveCellGraphs(pg_data)
pg_data <- pg_data |>
 LoadCellGraphs(cells = cells_of_interest) |>
 ComputeLayout(layout_method = "spectral") 
```

## 6.4. Fetch layout data

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_layout_data

layout_data <- FetchLayoutData(pg_data, 
  cells = cells_of_interest,
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  vars = markers_to_viz,
  add_marker = TRUE,
  layer = "counts")

```

## 6.4. Plot A single cell




## 6.4. 2D graph (markers × cells)

`Plot2DGraphM` draws one row per marker and one column per cell, coloured by marker
abundance. Colocalizing markers light up the same regions across cells.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_2d

layout_data |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(markers_to_viz), names_to = "marker_viz", values_to = "lps") |>
  cell_plot(color = lps) |>
  cell_node_scale_color(limits = c(0,2)) |>
  cell_grid(cols = component, rows = marker_viz)
```

## 6.5. Interactive 3D graph (one cell)

`Plot3DGraph` renders an interactive 3D view of one cell for one marker. Change
`cell_id` and `marker` to explore others.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_3d

Plot3DGraph(
  pg_data,
  cell_id       = cells_of_interest[1],
  marker        = markers_to_viz[1],
  layout_method = "cpmds_3d"
)
```

## 6.6. Render a 3D graph as a rotating .gif

`render_rotating_layout` exports the 3D layout as an animated GIF, with nodes
coloured by a marker's abundance. Useful for sharing a cell in slides or reports.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_3d_gif

cg <- CellGraphs(pg_data)[[cells_of_interest[1]]]

plot_data <-
  cg@layout$cpmds_3d |>
  mutate(node_val = cg@counts[, markers_to_viz[1]])

render_rotating_layout(
  plot_data,
  file = here::here("results/06_cell_visualization",
                    paste0(cell_type_of_interest, "_3d_rotation.gif")),
  colors           = c("gray90", "orangered"),
  pt_size          = 0.5,
  frames           = 20,
  max_degree       = 20,
  boomerang        = TRUE,
  use_illumination = TRUE,
  show_first_frame = FALSE
)
```
